record.title: Octopus proposes shared latent KV state for branching deep-search agents
record.summary: The Octopus preprint describes a GPU-resident key-value (KV) state directed acyclic graph for branching search, attention-only mounting of sibling branches and a packed DAG-GRPO training method. In experiments with Qwen3.5-4B, the authors report 49.6% on BrowseComp-Plus and 51.2% on OpenResearcher, alongside KV-mount retention and task-hijacking measurements, throughput and peak-memory comparisons. These are paper-reported results from a single-backbone setup, not independently reproduced.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper proposes Octopus, a GPU-resident key-value state DAG for branching multi-agent search. Its described operations include forking, thread reads/waits, rewind and commit/done, with zero-copy radix cursors and selective attention-KV mounting across branches.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Using Qwen3.5-4B with sparse BM25 retrieval, the authors report 49.6% on BrowseComp-Plus, 51.2% on OpenResearcher and a 17.5 percentage-point gain over their single-agent GRPO comparison. The reported regime uses 830 BrowseComp-Plus test queries and a 14.9-million-document OpenResearch corpus; these outcomes have not been independently reproduced.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that attention-only KV mounting retained 92.2% of answer information and produced 2.7% task hijacking, compared with 57.9% answer-information retention in their full-text condition; they also report 3.3× throughput and 2.8× peak KV-memory figures. These are paper-reported results, not independently verified measurements.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish independent reproduction, heterogeneous-backbone coordination, persistent memory, multi-node scaling to millions of agents, or generality beyond its reported single-backbone evaluation.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent matched reproduction of the BrowseComp-Plus, OpenResearcher, retention, hijacking, throughput or memory results was found or performed in this activation.
The paper links a public implementation repository, but this activation did not pin an immutable commit or inspect serving, KV-mount, trainer, evaluation code or tests.
The author metadata differs between the arXiv abstract page and full HTML author block.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported benchmark and systems results hold, shared latent KV state could materially improve the compute efficiency of multi-branch language-model search; the current evidence is one author-reported Qwen3.5-4B evaluation and does not establish independent reproduction or broader deployment regimes.
limitations: The reported results come from one Qwen3.5-4B backbone with sparse BM25 retrieval and bounded benchmark datasets.
No independent implementation audit or benchmark reproduction was performed in this activation.
The paper does not demonstrate heterogeneous multi-model operation, persistent memory, or multi-node scaling to millions of agents.
ArXiv abstract and full HTML list different author counts; attribution remains unresolved.
brief.summary: The Octopus preprint describes a GPU-resident key-value (KV) state directed acyclic graph for branching search, attention-only mounting of sibling branches and a packed DAG-GRPO training method. In experiments with Qwen3.5-4B, the authors report 49.6% on BrowseComp-Plus and 51.2% on OpenResearcher, alongside KV-mount retention and task-hijacking measurements, throughput and peak-memory comparisons. These are paper-reported results from a single-backbone setup, not independently reproduced.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report 49.6% BrowseComp-Plus and 51.2% OpenResearcher with Qwen3.5-4B; +17.5 percentage points versus their single-agent GRPO comparison; 92.2% answer-information retention and 2.7% task hijacking with attention-only mount versus 57.9% retention in the full-text condition; 3.3× throughput and 2.8× peak KV-memory figures. All remain paper-reported.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected arXiv primary record demonstrates that the preprint describes this mechanism and reports the stated evaluations. This activation did not independently verify implementation behavior or measured results.
technical.mechanism: A GPU-resident KV-state DAG shares latent attention state among branches of one search episode. The paper describes zero-copy radix cursors, branch operations and selective mounting of sibling attention KV while bypassing recurrent states; packed DAG-GRPO trains the branching policy.
technical.regime: One homogeneous Qwen3.5-4B backbone, sparse BM25 retrieval, 3,040 OpenResearch training queries, 500 validation queries, 830 BrowseComp-Plus test queries and a fixed 100,195-document BrowseComp-Plus corpus; paper also describes a 14.9-million-document OpenResearch corpus. Reported regime is episode-scoped KV state in single-node GPU pools, not heterogeneous or persistent multi-node deployment.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper’s stated single-agent GRPO Qwen3.5-4B comparison is the closest matched baseline for BrowseComp-Plus; the attention-only versus full-text mount comparison is the internal control for the context-transfer result. No independent matched baseline evaluation was performed.

brief.title: Octopus proposes shared latent KV state for branching deep-search agents
brief.why_it_matters: A shared latent KV substrate may let search branches reuse computation and context instead of duplicating full prompts. If the paper’s author-reported results survive matched independent evaluation, this could improve multi-step agent search efficiency; current evidence is limited to one model family and paper-reported benchmarks.
